summary: Unexpected elevated 5xx rate observed during background model sync and connection-throttle escalation
description: Issue summary: TextFlow reported a sustained increase in 5xx responses (~8-12% error rate) for their tenant between 11:30-13:20 PDT on 2026-03-12. Impact: customer-facing inference calls returned 502/504 intermittently; streaming sessions dropped with incomplete chunks. Environment: Dedicated tenant, reserved pool in us-west-2. Immediate business impact: degraded UX, elevated retry traffic from the customer side causing amplification.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer traffic pattern: steady concurrent streaming sessions (~350 concurrent connections) with a sudden background model sync job kicking at 11:28 PDT
2) Issue reproduced in production under similar concurrent streaming load when model-sync overlaps with tenant connection throttling event
3) Observed API gateway returning 502/504 while serving-runtime logs reported repeated session-manager timeouts and worker restarts
logs: apigw: 2026-03-12T11:31:02Z - upstream returned 502 - upstream: runtime-allocator-43 (http2 GOAWAY observed)
runtime: 2026-03-12T11:31:03Z - session_manager: write stalled for 12s; GPU worker pid=4123 killed (OOM-like memory fragmentation)
kv-cache: 2026-03-12T11:31:04Z - prefetch lock contention on tenant TextFlow (waiting_queue=14)
investigation_notes: 11:45 - Support triage: validated customer metrics and confirmed 5xx rate correlated with their tenant's reserved pool; other tenants in same pool showed minor increases but not as severe.
12:00 - SRE snapshot: concurrent worker restarts aligned with start of background model sync for a model snapshot refresh initiated by ops (internal job id: model-sync-20260312-60).

Hypothesis 1: Model sync induced temporary I/O and memory pressure on the host which increased scheduling latency and caused session-manager write starvation, leading to connection resets and 502s at API gateway.

Hypothesis 2: Tenant-level priority demotion/connection throttling logic ran concurrently (autoscaler scaling-down warm workers) and amplified prefetch lock contention for KV cache, producing retry storms.
Evidence: flamegraphs and GPU memory maps show fragmentation spikes during the window; kernel-level swap events were observed on host nodes servicing the tenant pool.
Correlation: A maintenance model-sync job was scheduled in the same availability zone at 11:28; rollback of that job coincided with error rate improvement.
Related signals: increased TLS handshake timeouts and http2 stream resets from apigw metrics; elevated queue depths on the runtime's incoming socket accept queue.
comments: Samira Patel (Support) 2026-03-12T11:40: We observed TextFlow reporting client-side retries and partial responses. Triage with SRE requested.
Diego Ramirez (SRE) 2026-03-12T11:55: Noted model-sync job running at same time. Scheduling I/O and memory pressure visible. Kicking off temporary mitigation: pause model-sync on implicated hosts.

Diego Ramirez (SRE) 2026-03-12T12:18: Paused model-sync job (model-sync-20260312-60), increased keepalive to 90s for tenant pool, patched session-manager to back off prefetch lock. Error rate fell from 11% to 0.8% over 20 minutes.
Samira Patel (Support) 2026-03-12T12:45: Customer confirms recovery and reduced retries. Providing follow-up plan and postmortem timeline.

resolution_notes: Mitigation executed: paused internal model-sync job on affected AZs, increased HTTP keepalive timeout for TextFlow tenant pool, and applied session-manager config change to reduce aggressive prefetch concurrency.

Permanent fix: engineering produced PR #4521 to add bounded prefetch semaphore and to avoid large synchronous model-sync I/O on worker hosts. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521

Rollout notes: PR to be staged in canary cluster; monitoring alert added for session-manager write stalls > 5s. Autoscaler policy updated to avoid scaling-down during model-sync windows for dedicated pools.
Customer follow-up: Offered post-incident review with TextFlow and scheduled a remediation window to validate the runtime patch on their reserved pool.

Postmortem action items: (1) Add model-sync blackout window for dedicated pools; (2) instrument GPU memory fragmentation metrics; (3) add automated detection for prefetch lock contention and circuit-breaker to avoid cascade retries.
Status: Resolved (temporary mitigations applied, PR opened for permanent fix).
